notes: Page 2 only shows assembling the Squidman minifigure (head/squid helmet, cape, torso, legs) and the finished Squidman and agent minifigures. Minifigure parts are not in the set's parts list, so no pieces are recorded.
The green banknote tile held by Squidman is shown, but it is not attached in a building step here.
Page 3 is the first building page (police vehicle). Step 1 places a black 2x4 plate (b1). Step 2 adds the white 2-finger hinge plate (b2) at one end of b1, with the fingers sticking out past the end.
I could not tell from the picture whether b2 sits on top of b1 or clutches it from underneath. I recorded b2 as resting on b1 and did not specify which studs it uses.

Step 3 adds two white 1x4 side-stud bricks (b3 and b4) side by side. b3 is the front brick with its side studs facing the viewer, and b4 is behind it with its side studs facing away. I inferred b4 from the 2x4 footprint and the parts list, because only the front brick is clearly visible.
The bricks sit on the black plate b1 and the white hinge plate b2.
Step 4 adds a white Technic brick (b5) on b1 at the end opposite the hinge, with its pin holes facing outward. Its exact stud positions on b1 are my best reading of the picture.

Step 5: a light bluish gray 2x3 plate (b6) goes on top of the white bricks. A blue Technic pin is pushed into a pin hole of b5. The picture shows a blue pin already in the other hole, so I recorded two pins (b7, b8), matching the 2x 4274 in the parts list.
Step 6: two trans-green cones (b9, b10) go onto the outer ends of the pins, like engine nozzles. This is my reading of the picture.

Step 6 also adds a white piece with a handle on top of b6. I read it as a 2540 side-handle plate (b11) resting on b6. The white area is larger than one 1x2 plate, so it may be a second part that I can't identify.
The 2x3 plate b6 probably covers the three right-hand columns of the brick block. I recorded it as resting on b3 and b4.

Sub-steps 1-2: a white curved wedge (the right one, 41747, b12) gets a dark gray grille tile (b13) on its two studs. A sticker is applied to the wedge's nose and its side ('POLICE'). I recorded the sticker as one part, b14, joined to b12.

Step 7: the wedge's underside holes go onto the four side studs of a 1x4 brick. I chose b4, the brick whose side studs face away from the front in step 3, because the arrows point at the opposite face from the cones. The picture could also mean b3.
I read the wedge's four visible holes as anti.1.1-4. The exact anti-stud positions are a guess.
Sub-steps 1-2 build the mirror of the previous wedge: the left curved wedge (41748, b15) with the second grille tile (b16) and a 'POLICE' sticker from the same sheet (b14).
Step 8 snaps b15 onto the four side studs of the other 1x4 brick, b3, on the opposite side of the model from b12. The grille tile is attached to the wedge's two studs.
As before, the wedge's anti-stud positions are a guess.

Step 9: two cheese slopes (trans-red b17 and trans-dark blue b18) go on the studs of the gray plate b6. A black clip tile (b19) also goes on b6. The white 2x2 flag (b20) clips onto the bar of the side-handle plate b11, so it lies flat on the left as a hatch.
I identified the flat hatch as the flag because it is the only flat 2x2 white part with a clip in the parts list. The step 9 picture does not label it.
Step 10: a red emblem sticker from the same sheet (b14) goes on the flag. The black handlebars (b21) clip into the clip tile b19.
The slopes and the clip tile are placed on b6, but I couldn't tell which studs from the picture. The exact stud positions are a guess.

Page 9 starts a second sub-model (the Squidman craft), shown as the small picture at the top left. Step 1: black 2x2 plate (b22). Step 2: a white hinge plate (b23) with its fingers sticking out. Step 3: red 2x2 plate (b24) on top. Step 4: two black brackets (b25, b26) on opposite sides.
The parts list has only one white 60471, and b2 on page 3 already used it. b23 may really be a different part, or b2 may have been misidentified. I used 60471 again and flag the over-count.
Step 4's view is unclear about exactly how the brackets attach. I recorded both as resting on the black plate b22 only. They may also clutch the red plate b24.
Step 5 looks like only a turn-over of the step 4 sub-assembly, so I recorded no new piece for it.
Step 6 adds two white sloped wedges (43710 and 43711). I set b27 on the bracket b25 and b28 on the bracket b26. I couldn't tell which wedge goes on which bracket.

Step 11 joins the new sub-assembly to the police craft. I read this as the sub-assembly's hinge b23 interlocking with the craft's hinge b2, since both have white fingers. The arrow does not show the join clearly, so this is an inference.
Step 12 only places the agent minifigure in the finished police craft, with its hands on the handlebars. Minifigures are not in the parts list, so no pieces or joins are recorded.
Page 12 is an advertising page for other Space Police sets (5969, 5970, 5971, 5972) and the minifigure characters. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 13 is an advertising page for Space Police sets 5973 and 5974 and more minifigures. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 14 is the parts inventory and customer service page. It has no building step, so nothing is added.

The inventory shows a single white 2-finger hinge (4515337) and a single black 1-finger hinge (4185620). Pages 3 and 9 each show a hinge with white fingers, but the set has only one white 2-finger hinge. The repeated use of 60471 (b2 and b23) may therefore be an over-count, and one of them may be the black 1-finger hinge 44567a.
Page 15 is a LEGO Club and LEGO Shop advertisement. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 16 is a survey and prize advertisement. It has no building step, so nothing is added.

The 15 separate groups came from my own earlier omission: I recorded the stacking joins (pieces resting on others) in my notes but never as edges. This turn adds them as stud/anti-stud 'joined' edges. The model is one build: the police craft, with the second sub-assembly hinged to it.

The exact stud and anti-stud positions in these joins are my best reading of the small pictures. I kept each join consistent with the piece's catalogue ports and the step order. To avoid a level conflict I put the hinge b2 under plate b1, and the hinge b23 under plate b22.
b23 is corrected from 60471 to 44567a, the black 1-finger hinge. The inventory has one white 2-finger hinge (b2) and one black 1-finger hinge. This keeps the part counts right.

Pieces I could not locate in the pictures: the parts-list counts require 2 more side-handle plates 2540 (b29, b30), a second black 2x4 plate (b31), the white jumper plate 3794b (b33) and the green '100' tile (b32). I placed them where the pictures show unexplained white or black pieces.

b33 is the white jumper plate under the white area on the gray plate b6, with the clip tile b19 on its stud. b29 and b30 are on the bracket studs of the second sub-assembly. b31 is a base plate under b22. These three are guesses.
b32 is the green '100' banknote tile. Squidman holds it on page 2, so it has no brick join. It stays unattached on purpose and is not an assembly error.
Parts only in the minifigure pages (page 2, page 12) are not in the parts list and are not modelled.

The two groups are the assembled police craft (everything joined, including the hinged second sub-assembly) and b32, the green '100' banknote tile. I am keeping b32 separate because it is a loose accessory. Page 2 shows Squidman holding it in his hand, and no building step attaches it to any brick. Adding a join would invent a connection the booklet doesn't show.
The minifigures are not in the parts list, so b32 has nothing to join to in the graph. Nothing else is added in this turn.
